decks.name: LeetCode #105 - Construct Binary Tree from Preorder and Inorder Traversal
decks.description: Construct binary tree from preorder and inorder traversal arrays

cards.question: Construct Binary Tree from Preorder and Inorder Traversal: Given two integer arrays preorder and inorder where preorder is the preorder traversal of a binary tree and inorder is the inorder traversal of the same tree, construct and return the binary tree.

solutions.name: Depth First Search
solutions.explanation: Use recursive DFS to build tree from traversal arrays. Root is always first element in preorder. Find root position in inorder to determine left and right subtree boundaries. Elements before root in inorder form left subtree, elements after form right subtree. Recursively build left subtree with corresponding preorder and inorder slices, then right subtree. O(n²) time due to repeated indexOf operations and array slicing.

solutions.name: Hash Map + Depth First Search
solutions.explanation: Optimize with hash map for O(1) root position lookup in inorder. Pre-build indices map from inorder array. Use single preorder index counter (pre_idx) incremented as we build nodes. Helper function dfs(l, r) takes boundaries in inorder array. Get current root from preorder, increment counter, find position in inorder using map, recursively build left and right subtrees with adjusted boundaries. O(n) time, O(n) space.

solutions.name: Depth First Search (Optimal)
solutions.explanation: Most space-efficient approach using two pointers (preIdx, inIdx) and limit parameter. No hash map or array slicing needed. Limit represents boundary value - when inorder[inIdx] matches limit, we've completed current subtree and backtrack. Build root from preorder, recursively build left subtree with root value as limit, then right subtree with current limit. Indices advance naturally as tree is constructed. O(n) time, O(n) space for recursion stack only.

solutions.exampleWalkthrough: Given preorder=[3,9,20,15,7] and inorder=[9,3,15,20,7]: dfs(inf): root=3 (preIdx=0 to 1). Left: dfs(3): root=9 (preIdx=1 to 2), left tries dfs(9) but inorder[0]=9 matches limit, returns null, right tries dfs(3) but inorder[1]=3 matches limit, returns null. Right: dfs(inf): root=20 (preIdx=2 to 3), left=dfs(20): root=15, right=dfs(inf): root=7. Returns complete tree.
